subject: Request: guarded edge topology + connectivity matrix for SOC 2 review
messages:

Subject: Request: guarded edge topology + connectivity matrix for SOC 2 review

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this — our SOC 2 audit team asked specifically for a low-level connectivity matrix and an edge/topology summary for Redwood's Private and Dedicated deployment options. The auditors want: 1) which ports/protocols are used for control plane vs data plane, 2) where egress exits to customer networks vs internet, 3) whether per-tenant routing or shared overlay is used, and 4) a simple diagram we can include in the narrative.

Can you provide a PDF or PNG we can append to the report, plus a CSV matrix that enumerates each service endpoint and required outbound/ inbound ports?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — audit window is next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Orion Health

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are two artefacts to start: 1) guarded-edge-topology-v1.pdf — a concise diagram showing the Private and Dedicated variants, control vs data plane segregation, and default egress points; 2) connectivity-matrix-20270503.csv — a row-per-endpoint CSV with ports/protocols, typical source/destination, and notes on per-tenant isolation.

High-level callouts:
- Control plane (customer-management, model registry, orchestration) always routes via the Redwood control plane endpoint over mutual TLS; for Private deployments that control plane can be run in-customer VPC or routed over a private peering circuit.
- Data plane (inference requests / streaming) is pinned to region-specific edge clusters; for Dedicated we provide a dedicated GPU pool with per-pool egress controls; for Private you may opt for routed-only egress through your NAT.
- We use per-tenant overlay networks inside Dedicated pools by default; Private gives customers the option to use their own VPC subnets and route tables.

Vivek and Karthik are copied for technical confirmation; happy to iterate quickly if the auditors need more granularity.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Alex — quick technical clarifications to annotate the diagram and CSV:

1) Ports and protocols
   - Control plane API: 443 (mutual TLS, client cert auth).
   - Model artifact registry: 443 (HTTPS) to S3-compatible endpoint; if Private-on-prem we also support signed NFS mounts — noted in CSV.
   - Inference data plane: 443 (HTTP/2 gRPC optional) for request/response; streaming uses HTTP/1.1 chunked in hosted flows.

2) Egress behavior
   - Dedicated: egress is NATed via the dedicated pool's egress IP(s); customers can provide IP allowlists.
   - Private (VPC mode): egress follows customer route tables; if you enable private-only mode, there is zero direct internet egress from the inference nodes.

3) Tenant isolation model
   - Dedicated: logical tenant isolation via per-tenant namespaces and network policies within the pool; default overlay prevents cross-tenant east-west unless explicitly configured for private peering.
   - Private: tenant traffic stays in your network; Redwood agents bind to customer subnets.

I'll attach a small annotated PNG with the control/data plane arrows and a short legend you can drop into the audit evidence.

-Vivek
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Alex —

Short answers for auditors (feel free to paste):

1) Dedicated egress IPs: we publish dedicated-pool egress CIDR lists per-region once a pool is provisioned; for audit purposes we provided a conservative reference list in the CSV under the column "egress_reference_cidr". If you need a fixed list for a particular Dedicated commitment, we can provide the exact CIDR/elastic IPs tied to that contract.

2) Persistent storage of inference payloads: no. By default Redwood does not persist raw inference payloads in the control plane. We log request metadata (timestamps, token counts, route IDs) for observability and billing; payloads may be cached briefly in-memory or KV stores for prefix caching but are not written to long-term control-plane storage. Retention for metadata logs is 90 days by default and can be extended under enterprise contracts.

I've also added a short note to guarded-edge-topology-v1.pdf (v1.1) clarifying the retention and egress guidance — link below.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cGuardedEdge

Happy to jump on a call if auditors want to review the diagram live.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
